config.title: Build typed plugin system

intro.title: Build typed plugin system
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed plugin system for a simple application. You will learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define a contract that all plugins must follow. This involves creating a plugin manager that can register and run different plugins while ensuring type safety. By the end, you'll understand how to structure a flexible, extensible system with strict type checking.
intro.usecase: Typed plugin systems are essential in modern applications where extensibility is required without compromising type safety. In developer tools like VS Code or Figma, plugins for syntax highlighting, linting rules, or design components rely on typed interfaces to ensure compatibility. Content management systems like WordPress use typed plugin architectures to safely extend functionality with custom blocks, widgets, and APIs. Even in enterprise dashboards, typed plugins allow teams to add custom charts, data sources, or authentication modules while maintaining reliable integration through TypeScript's type checking.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface that defines the required shape for all plugins
Implement a concrete plugin class that satisfies the defined interface
Initialize a plugin registry that stores and manages typed plugin instances
Apply type guards to validate plugin objects at runtime
Integrate the plugin system into a host application with proper type safety
Manipulate the plugin registry to add, remove, and retrieve plugins
Configure the plugin system to support dynamic loading of typed plugins

steps.title: Import TypeScript types and interfaces
steps.instruction: Import the TypeScript types and interfaces needed for the plugin system. Add the following imports at the top of your file: `Plugin`, `PluginConfig`, and `PluginRegistry` from './types'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from the './types' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple named exports
import { User, Profile, Settings } from './models';
steps.seedCode: // Import the required types and interfaces here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary type imports for building the typed plugin system.
successCriteria: The imports for Plugin, PluginConfig, and PluginRegistry from './types' are present.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but not all required imports are present. Make sure to import Plugin, PluginConfig, and PluginRegistry from './types'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required imports are missing. Please import Plugin, PluginConfig, and PluginRegistry from './types'.

steps.title: Define Plugin interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'Plugin' with two properties: 'name' (string) and 'execute' (function that returns void).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required types and interfaces here

// Create the Plugin interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Plugin interface is defined with the correct structure.
successCriteria: The Plugin interface exists with 'name: string' and 'execute: () => void' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface has both 'name' (string) and 'execute' (function returning void) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Plugin interface is not correctly defined. Check that you used the 'interface' keyword and included both required properties.

steps.title: Define PluginRegistry type
steps.instruction: Create a type named PluginRegistry using TypeScript's Record type to map string keys to Plugin values.
steps.hint: Use the syntax: type PluginRegistry = Record<string, Plugin>;
steps.expectedOutcome: A PluginRegistry type is defined that enforces all values to be of type Plugin.
successCriteria: PluginRegistry is defined as a type using Record<string, Plugin>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using Record<string, Plugin> to define the PluginRegistry type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PluginRegistry type wasn't defined correctly. Try using Record<string, Plugin> to create the type.

steps.title: Initialize plugin registry
steps.instruction: Initialize a constant named 'pluginRegistry' with the PluginRegistry type and set it to an empty object.
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword, the type annotation syntax with a colon, and assign an empty object {}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: typed empty object
const userData: UserProfile = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed empty object is created and ready to store plugins.
successCriteria: A constant named 'pluginRegistry' is declared with the PluginRegistry type and initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared a constant with the correct name and type, and assigned an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The plugin registry initialization is missing or incorrect. Check the name, type annotation, and assignment.

steps.title: Create registerPlugin function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'registerPlugin' that takes a parameter of type 'Plugin' and adds it to the 'pluginRegistry' object.
steps.hint: The function should accept a plugin parameter and assign it to the registry using the plugin's name as the key.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that registers plugins into the type-safe registry is implemented.
successCriteria: The 'registerPlugin' function is defined, accepts a 'Plugin' parameter, and adds it to 'pluginRegistry' using the plugin's name as key.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but check that it properly adds the plugin to the registry using the plugin's name as the key.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't correctly register plugins. Ensure it accepts a Plugin parameter and adds it to pluginRegistry.

steps.title: Create getPlugin function
steps.instruction: Create a function named getPlugin that takes a plugin name as a string parameter and returns the corresponding plugin from the registry, or undefined if not found.
steps.hint: Define a function that accesses the pluginRegistry object using the provided name as a key.
steps.expectedOutcome: A getPlugin function is added that retrieves plugins from the registry in a type-safe manner.
successCriteria: The getPlugin function is defined with proper TypeScript parameter and return types, and correctly accesses the pluginRegistry.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the getPlugin function, but check the parameter type, return type, or registry access logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getPlugin function is missing or incorrect. Ensure it takes a string parameter and returns a plugin or undefined from pluginRegistry.

steps.title: Create executePlugin function
steps.instruction: Create a function named executePlugin that takes a plugin name and an optional input,
steps.hint: The function should accept a plugin name (string) and an optional input parameter, retrieve the plugin using getPlugin, and call its execute method if the plugin exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new executePlugin function is added to the codebase with proper TypeScript typing for plugin execution.
successCriteria: The executePlugin function is defined, accepts a plugin name and optional input, uses getPlugin to retrieve the plugin, and calls its execute method with type safety.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your executePlugin function accepts the correct parameters, retrieves the plugin using getPlugin, and calls its execute method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The executePlugin function is missing or incorrect. Review the function signature and ensure it properly retrieves and executes plugins with TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Create sample plugins
steps.instruction: Create two sample plugin objects that implement the Plugin interface. Name them 'loggerPlugin' and 'calculatorPlugin'.
steps.hint: Define each plugin as a constant object with the required properties from the Plugin interface: name, version, and execute.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two plugin objects are created with proper type annotations and implementations.
successCriteria: Two constants named 'loggerPlugin' and 'calculatorPlugin' are defined, both typed as Plugin, with name, version, and execute properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created at least one plugin, but make sure to create both 'loggerPlugin' and 'calculatorPlugin' with all required properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample plugins are not correctly implemented. Ensure both plugins have name, version, and execute properties and are typed as Plugin.

steps.title: Register sample plugins
steps.instruction: Call the registerPlugin function to register both sample plugins you created earlier.
steps.hint: You need to call registerPlugin twice - once for each plugin object. Pass the plugin object as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both sample plugins should be registered in the plugin registry using the registerPlugin function.
successCriteria: The registerPlugin function is called twice with the correct plugin objects as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've registered at least one plugin, but make sure to register both sample plugins you created earlier.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample plugins aren't registered yet. Call the registerPlugin function for each plugin object.

steps.title: Test plugin execution
steps.instruction: Call the executePlugin function for both registered plugins and log the results to verify type-safe behavior.
steps.hint: Use console.log to output the results of executing each plugin by name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The console will show the output from both plugins: 'Hello, World!' from the 'greet' plugin and 15 from the 'multiply' plugin.
successCriteria: Both plugins are executed using executePlugin and their results are logged to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling executePlugin for both registered plugins ('greet' and 'multiply') and logging the results.
